questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes 6 min 40 s to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is:
questions.solution_text: Time, $t = 6\,\text{min}\,40\,\text{s} = 360 + 40 = 400\,\text{s}$. Since speed of light $v = 1$ (new unit), distance $d = vt = 1 \times 400 = 400$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Young's Modulus, Compressibility, Bulk Modulus, Poisson's Ratio
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II: | List I | List II | |---|---| | A. Young's Modulus | I. $\dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L}\left(\dfrac{L}{d}\right)$ | | B. Compressibility | II. $\dfrac{FL}{A(\Delta L)}$ | | C. Bulk Modulus | III. $-\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ | | D. Poisson's Ratio | IV. $-P\left(\dfrac{V}{\Delta V}\right)$ |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Young's Modulus $= \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} = \dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}$ (II). Compressibility $= \dfrac{1}{\text{Bulk modulus}} = -\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\right)$ (III). Bulk Modulus $= -P\left(\dfrac{V}{\Delta V}\right)$ (IV). Poisson's Ratio $= \dfrac{\text{Lateral strain}}{\text{Longitudinal strain}} = \dfrac{\Delta d}{\Delta L}\left(\dfrac{L}{d}\right)$ (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The current $I$ in the circuit shown below is (All diodes are ideal and identical). The circuit has four parallel branches between two nodes connected to a 10 V battery: a $4\,\Omega$ resistor with a diode oriented to conduct, a $3\,\Omega$ resistor with a diode oriented to block (reverse biased), a $2\,\Omega$ resistor with a diode oriented to conduct, and a $5\,\Omega$ resistor with a diode oriented to block (reverse biased).
questions.solution_text: For an ideal diode, forward resistance $= 0$ and reverse-biased resistance $= \infty$. So the branches with reverse-biased diodes (the $3\,\Omega$ and $5\,\Omega$ branches) carry no current and can be removed. The circuit reduces to two parallel branches of $4\,\Omega$ and $2\,\Omega$ across a 10 V source. Total current $I = \dfrac{10}{2} + \dfrac{10}{4} = 5 + 2.5 = \dfrac{30}{4} = \dfrac{15}{2}\,A$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.subtopic: Angular Acceleration and Number of Revolutions
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from 600 rpm to 1200 rpm in 10 s. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
questions.solution_text: $\omega_1 = 600 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 20\pi\,\text{rad/s}$, $\omega_2 = 1200 \times \dfrac{2\pi}{60} = 40\pi\,\text{rad/s}$. Using $\omega_2^2 = \omega_1^2 + 2\alpha\theta$: $(40\pi)^2 = (20\pi)^2 + 2\alpha\theta$, where $\alpha = \dfrac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{20\pi}{10} = 2\pi\,\text{rad/s}^2$. So $1200\pi^2 = 4\pi\theta \Rightarrow \theta = 300\pi$ radians. Number of revolutions $= \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{300\pi}{2\pi} = 150$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a simple pendulum, having time period $T$, the variation of kinetic energy (K.E.) with time ($t$) is represented by one of four graphs labelled (1) to (4), each showing K.E. on the y-axis and $t$ on the x-axis with markings at $T/2$ and $T$. Which graph correctly represents this variation?

options.text: Graph (1): K.E. constant (flat line) from $0$ to $T$
Graph (2): K.E. is a positive sinusoidal curve above the axis with period $T/2$, never touching zero
Graph (3): K.E. is $\cos^2$-type curve touching zero at $t=0$, $T/2$, $T$ with maxima between these points
Graph (4): K.E. is a curve starting positive at $t=0$, decreasing to zero at $T/2$ then increasing again to $T$, shifted from graph (3)

questions.solution_text: Kinetic energy $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)$. Therefore $K \propto \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)$, which is always non-negative, oscillates with period $T/2$ (since $\cos^2$ has half the period of $\cos$), and touches zero twice every full period $T$ — at $t=0$, $T/2$, and $T$. This matches the curve described in option (3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A resistor is connected to a battery of 12 V emf and internal resistance $2\,\Omega$. If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
questions.solution_text: Terminal voltage of battery $V = E - ir = 12 - 0.6 \times 2 = 12 - 1.2 = 10.8\,V$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Comparison of RMS Speeds of Two Gases
questions.question_text: A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of $2:1$ by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $27^\circ C$. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases $\left(\dfrac{V_{rms}^{Ar}}{V_{rms}^{Cl}}\right)$ is: (Atomic mass of argon = 40.0 u and molecular mass of chlorine = 70.0 u)
questions.solution_text: $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$. For the same temperature, $v_{rms} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$. So $\dfrac{V_{rms}^{Ar}}{V_{rms}^{Cl}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_{Cl}}{M_{Ar}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{70}{40}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$. Note: the mass ratio given (2:1) is extra information not needed for this ratio since $v_{rms}$ depends only on molar mass and temperature, not on the amount of gas.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ray of monochromatic light is passing through an equilateral prism (ABC) as shown in the figure. The refracted ray (QR) is parallel to its base (BC) and the angle of incidence ($i$) is $50^\circ$. Then the angle of deviation ($\delta$) is:
questions.solution_text: Since the refracted ray QR is parallel to the base BC, the prism is at minimum deviation condition, so $i = e = 50^\circ$. Using the prism equation $i + e = A + \delta$, and since $i=e$: $2i - A = \delta \Rightarrow 2(50) - 60 = \delta \Rightarrow \delta = 40^\circ$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon Energy, de Broglie Wavelength, Compton Effect
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II: | List-I | List-II | |---|---| | A. $E = h\nu$ | I. de Broglie wavelength | | B. Diffraction and Interference | II. Particle nature of light | | C. $\lambda = h/p$ | III. Wave nature of light | | D. Compton effect | IV. Energy of photon |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: $E = h\nu$ represents the energy of photon (IV). Diffraction and interference confirm wave nature of light (III). $\lambda = h/p$ is the de Broglie wavelength of a particle (I). The Compton effect confirms the particle nature of light (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is $-3.4\,eV$. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately: (Take $1\,eV = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,J$, $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\,C$ and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}\,N\,m^2/C^2$)
questions.solution_text: The energy is related to the radius by $\dfrac{KQ^2}{2r} = 3.4\,eV$ (in magnitude), where $K = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$. So $r = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{2 \times 3.4 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$. Calculating: $r = 2.1176 \times 10^{-10}\,m \approx 2.1 \times 10^{-10}\,m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A box of mass 15 kg is kept on the floor of a stationary trolley. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the trolley is 0.12. Keeping the box in stationary state over the trolley, the maximum acceleration with which the trolley can be moved horizontally in $m\,s^{-2}$ is: ($g = 10\,m/s^2$)
questions.solution_text: For the box to remain stationary relative to the trolley, the maximum acceleration is limited by the maximum available friction force: $a = \mu g = 0.12 \times 10 = 1.2\,m/s^2$. (Mass of box is not needed since $a = \mu g$ is independent of mass.)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Five capacitors of capacitances $C_1 = C_2 = C_3 = C_4 = 10\,\mu F$ and $C_5 = 2.5\,\mu F$ are connected as shown, along with a battery of 50 V. The capacitors $C_2$ and $C_3$ are in series forming one branch, $C_1$ is in another branch, $C_4$ is in another branch, all connected in a network, with $C_5$ connected separately across the battery of 50 V. The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor respectively are:
questions.solution_text: The combination of $C_1, C_2, C_3, C_4$ (each $10\,\mu F$) reduces to an equivalent of $2.5\,\mu F$, and this is in series/parallel arrangement with $C_5 = 2.5\,\mu F$ such that $C_{eq} = 2.5 + 2.5 = 5\,\mu F$. With 50 V applied, $q_1 = q_2 = q_3 = q_4 = 2.5 \times 50 = 125\,\mu C$ and $q_5 = 2.5 \times 50 = 125\,\mu C$. So all capacitors carry $125\,\mu C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Work Done to Raise a Mass
questions.question_text: The amount of work done to raise a mass '$m$' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth '$R$' will be:
questions.solution_text: $W.D. = U_2 - U_1 = -\dfrac{GMm}{R+R} - \left(-\dfrac{GMm}{R}\right) = -\dfrac{GMm}{2R} + \dfrac{GMm}{R} = \dfrac{GMm}{2R} = \dfrac{mgR}{2}$ (using $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Each side of a metallic cube of mass 5.580 kg is measured to be 9.0 cm. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as $X \times 10^3\,kg\,m^{-3}$ where the value of $X$ is:
questions.solution_text: Density $= \dfrac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} = \dfrac{5.580\,kg}{(9.0\,cm)^3} = \dfrac{5.580}{729} \times 10^6\,\dfrac{kg}{m^3} = 0.007654321 \times 10^6\,\dfrac{kg}{m^3} = 7.654 \times 10^3\,\dfrac{kg}{m^3}$. Since the side length (9.0 cm) has only 2 significant figures, the result should be rounded to 2 significant figures: $X = 7.7$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The following plots (A, B, C, D, E) show variation of velocity ($v$) with time ($t$) of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Plot A: $v$ starts at a positive value, increases to a peak, then decreases to a negative value by time $T$. Plot B: $v$ starts at a positive value, increases linearly to a peak at $T/2$, then decreases linearly back to the starting positive value at $T$ (triangle shape, all positive). Plot C: $v$ starts at a positive value at $t=0$ and decreases linearly (constant negative slope) throughout to a negative value at $T$. Plot D: $v$ starts at zero and increases linearly to a positive value at $T$. Plot E: $v$ starts at a high positive value, decreases to a minimum around some point, then increases again, always positive (U-shaped curve). Which of the following plots is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: During the whole journey (going up and coming down), the acceleration due to gravity acts vertically downward throughout. Therefore, the slope of the velocity-time graph (which represents acceleration) should be negative (constant) throughout the journey, going from a positive initial velocity (upward) to a negative final velocity (downward) at landing. This matches plot (C).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is 0.02 joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately: (Consider mass of the bob = 20 g)
questions.solution_text: At the equilibrium position, total energy = kinetic energy (potential energy is zero there). So $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.02$. With $m = 20\,g = 20 \times 10^{-3}\,kg$: $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 10^{-3} \times v^2 = 0.02 \Rightarrow v^2 = 2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\,m/s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is $\lambda$, is $K$ units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$ will be:
questions.solution_text: The intensity is given by $I = I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\Delta\phi}{2}\right)$, where $\Delta\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x$. For path difference $\lambda$: $\Delta\phi = 2\pi$, so $K = I_0\cos^2(\pi) = I_0$. For path difference $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$: $\Delta\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$, so $I_1 = I_0\cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = I_0 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{4} = \dfrac{K}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In the circuit shown below, an AC source $V_i$ is connected in series with a diode $D$ and a resistor $R$, with $V_D$ being the voltage measured across the diode. The voltage appearing across the diode $D$ will be of the form:

options.text: Two full positive humps of $v_D$ vs $t$ with no negative portion (full-wave rectified appearance)
A full sine wave of $v_D$ vs $t$, both positive and negative halves shown normally
Two positive humps separated by flat zero regions, repeating, with no negative parts shown
One positive hump followed by a flat line at zero (only one half cycle shown as a bump, rest flat)

questions.solution_text: There is a voltage drop across the diode only when it is in reverse bias (since it offers very high resistance then, and almost all the source voltage appears across it). During the positive half cycle, the diode is reverse biased, so the voltage $V_D$ shows a hump (mirroring the input). During the negative half cycle, the diode is forward biased (conducting), so it has negligible voltage drop (flat at zero). This corresponds to option (4): one positive hump then a flat line.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An ac circuit contains a resistance of 1 k$\Omega$, a capacitor of 0.1 $\mu$F and an inductor of 1 mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately:
questions.solution_text: Resonance frequency $f_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$. With $L = 1\times 10^{-3}\,H$ and $C = 0.1\,\mu F = 1 \times 10^{-7}\,F$: $f_0 = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{1 \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{-3}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-10}}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \times 10^{-5}} \approx 15.9\,kHz$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. If it reduces in one region, producing a dark fringe, it increases in another region, producing a bright fringe.

A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy.

B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true and B is also true
A is false, but B is true
A is true, but B is false
Both A and B are false

questions.solution_text: In interference and diffraction, there is no loss of energy — energy is merely redistributed, so statement A is true. However, diffraction and interference are exhibited by all types of waves (including sound waves), not just light waves, so statement B is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a travelling harmonic wave $y(x,t) = 2.0\cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ in s. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of $0.5\,m$ is:
questions.solution_text: The phase is $\phi = 20\pi - 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3}x + 2\pi \times 0.35$ (rewriting $0.0080x = 8 \times 10^{-3}x$, all distances in cm). Phase difference $\Delta\phi = k\Delta x = 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times \Delta x$. Converting $\Delta x = 0.5\,m = 50\,cm$: $\Delta\phi = 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times 50 = 2\pi \times 0.4 = 0.8\pi$. So $\Delta\phi = 0.8\pi\,rad$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass 5 kg when two mutually perpendicular forces 8 N and 6 N act on it, are respectively:
questions.solution_text: Net force $F_{net} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36+64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\,N$. Acceleration $a = \dfrac{F_{net}}{m} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2\,m/s^2$. The angle with the 8 N force: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{6}{8} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)$ from the 8 N force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance 200 pF. One of them is charged by a 100 V supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is:
questions.solution_text: Energy loss $= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C_1C_2}{C_1+C_2}V^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{200 \times 200}{400}\right) \times 10^{-12} \times (100)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 \times 10^{-12} \times 10^4 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10^{-6} = 0.5 \times 10^{-6}\,J$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is: ($g = 9.8\,m/s^2$)
questions.solution_text: Power $= \dfrac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}} = \dfrac{mgh}{t} = \dfrac{10^3 \times 9.8 \times 20}{10} = \dfrac{196000}{10} = 19600\,W = 19.6\,kW$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a vernier calliper, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier callipers is:
questions.solution_text: Least count $= 1\,MSD - 1\,VSD$. Given $20\,VSD = 16\,MSD \Rightarrow 1\,VSD = \dfrac{16}{20}\,MSD$. So $L.C. = 1\,MSD - \dfrac{16}{20}\,MSD = \dfrac{4}{20}\,MSD = \dfrac{1}{5}\,mm = 0.2\,mm = 0.02\,cm$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. ($g = 9.8\,m\,s^{-2}$)

A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s. B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s.

C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s. D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s.

E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s.

What is the correct order of the distance travelled by the ruler for each person?
questions.solution_text: Distance fallen under gravity $s = \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$, which increases with reaction time $t$. Since larger reaction time means larger distance travelled, ordering the reaction times in descending order: $t_B (0.22) > t_E (0.21) > t_A (0.20) > t_D (0.19) > t_C (0.18)$. Thus the distance order is $S_B > S_E > S_A > S_D > S_C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Balanced Bridge in a Square Loop
questions.question_text: A uniform metallic wire having resistance $4\,\Omega$ is bent to form a square loop (ABCD) (see figure). A resistance of $2\,\Omega$ is connected between points B and D and a battery of 2 V is connected across points A and C as shown in the figure. Now the value of current ($I$) is:
questions.solution_text: Each side of the square has resistance $\dfrac{4}{4} = 1\,\Omega$. The arrangement forms a balanced Wheatstone bridge with the $2\,\Omega$ resistor as the bridge element between B and D, so no current flows through the $2\,\Omega$ resistor. The effective resistance between A and C (through the two parallel paths of $1+1=2\,\Omega$ each) is $\dfrac{2 \times 2}{2+2} = 1\,\Omega$. Current $I = \dfrac{E}{R_{eff}} = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2\,A$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?
questions.solution_text: Since $P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}$ and $R$ remains constant, $\dfrac{P_c}{P_0} = \dfrac{V^2}{V_0^2}$. So $P_c = \left(\dfrac{V}{V_0}\right)^2 P_0 = \left(\dfrac{200}{220}\right)^2 \times 400 \approx 0.8264 \times 400 \approx 331\,W$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of $3.14 \times 10^{-3}\,T$ at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively: (Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\,T\,m/A$)
questions.solution_text: Magnetic field at centre $B_0 = \dfrac{\mu_0 Ni}{2R} \Rightarrow i = \dfrac{2RB_0}{\mu_0 N} = \dfrac{2 \times 5\times10^{-2} \times 3.14\times10^{-3}}{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 100} = 2.5\,A$. Magnetic moment $M = NiA = 100 \times 2.5 \times 3.14 \times (5\times10^{-2})^2 = 2\,A\,m^2$ (using $A=\pi R^2$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: EMF Across Rectangular Loop Moving Out of Field
questions.question_text: A rectangular wire loop of sides 8 cm and 3 cm with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.3 T directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is $2\,cm\,s^{-1}$, in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be:
questions.solution_text: When the velocity is normal to the shorter side, the relevant length for induced emf is the longer side (3 cm... actually the side perpendicular to velocity contributes). $E_{induced} = Bvl$, where $l$ is the length of the side perpendicular to the velocity. Here $E = 0.3 \times (2 \times 10^{-2}) \times (3 \times 10^{-2}) = 1.8 \times 10^{-4}\,V$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Volume Proportionality and Mass Defect Definition
questions.question_text:
Four statements are given ($A$ is mass number):

A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A^{1/3}$.

B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.

C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.

D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A and C are true, but B and D are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
A and D are true, but B and C are false
B and D are true, but A and C are false

questions.solution_text: The radius of a nucleus is $r = r_0 A^{1/3}$, so $r^3 \propto A$, and since $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, we get $V \propto A$ (statement B correct, A incorrect). The mass defect is defined as the difference between the mass of a nucleus and the sum of masses of its constituent nucleons (statement D correct, C incorrect — C describes binding energy related concept incorrectly).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Mass Number from Density and Mass
questions.question_text: An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of $2.29 \times 10^{17}\,kg/m^3$ and mass of $19.926 \times 10^{-27}\,kg$. Its mass number $A$ is approximately: (Take $R_0 = 1.2 \times 10^{-15}\,m$, $4\pi = 12.56$)
questions.solution_text: Using $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V}$ and $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$: $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = \dfrac{M}{\rho} \Rightarrow \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A = \dfrac{M}{\rho} \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{M}{\rho} \times \dfrac{3}{4\pi R_0^3} = \dfrac{19.926\times10^{-27} \times 3}{2.29\times10^{17} \times 12.56 \times (1.2\times10^{-15})^3} \approx 12$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum $L$, notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as 60 s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (Take $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8\,m/s^2$)
questions.solution_text: Time period $T = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2\,s$. From $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$, we get $l = \dfrac{gT^2}{4\pi^2} = \dfrac{9.8 \times 2 \times 2}{4 \times 9.8} = \dfrac{39.2}{39.2} = 1\,m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Rate of Change of Internal Energy
questions.question_text: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of 100 W. If the system performs work at a rate of 75 J/s, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
questions.solution_text: Using the first law of thermodynamics: $\dfrac{dQ}{dt} = \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + \dfrac{dW}{dt}$. So $100\,W = \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + 75\,W \Rightarrow \dfrac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} = 25\,W$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A thin wire of length '$L$' and linear mass density '$m$' is bent into a circular ring (in $x$-$y$ plane) with centre '$C$' as shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the ring about an axis $yy'$ (a tangent line in the plane of the ring, perpendicular to $x$-axis, passing through a point on the circumference) will be:
questions.solution_text: Mass of the ring $M = mL$, and $L = 2\pi r \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{L}{2\pi}$. The moment of inertia about a diameter is $I_{CM} = \dfrac{Mr^2}{2}$. Using the parallel axis theorem for the tangent axis $yy'$ (perpendicular distance $r$ from CM): $I_{yy'} = I_{CM} + Mr^2 = \dfrac{Mr^2}{2} + Mr^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}Mr^2$. Substituting $M=mL$ and $r=\dfrac{L}{2\pi}$: $I_{yy'} = \dfrac{3}{2}(mL)\left(\dfrac{L}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3mL^3}{8\pi^2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A galvanometer of resistance 100 $\Omega$ gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0 – 10 A. The shunt required is:
questions.solution_text: $i_G = 1\,mA = 0.001\,A$, $i_S = 10 - i_G \approx 10\,A$. Since shunt and galvanometer are in parallel, $i_S r_S = i_G R_G \Rightarrow 10 \times r_S = 0.001 \times 100 \Rightarrow r_S = 0.01\,\Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Effect of Interchanging Cell and Galvanometer
questions.question_text: In a metre bridge experiment (see figure), the positions of the cell, $E$, and galvanometer, $G$, are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:

options.text: There will be no deflection irrespective of the position of the jockey
Both right-sided and left-sided deflection and at balance point, no deflection

questions.solution_text: The position of the null (balance) point does not change when the galvanometer ($G$) and the cell ($E$) are interchanged. There will be zero deflection in the galvanometer only at the balance point. At unbalanced positions of the jockey, the deflection may be towards the left side or the right side depending on the jockey's position relative to balance point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The peak value of an alternating current is 5 A and frequency is 60 Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
questions.solution_text: $i = i_{peak}\sin(\omega t)$, where $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 60 = 120\pi\,rad/s$. For $i = i_{peak}$: $\sin(120\pi t) = 1 = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \Rightarrow 120\pi t = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{1}{240}\,s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Wire
questions.subtopic: B vs r for Solid Cylindrical Conductor
questions.question_text: The figure given below shows a long straight solid wire of circular cross-section of radius '$a$' carrying steady current $I$. The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The plot which correctly represents the variation of magnetic field ($B$) with distance ($r$) from the axis of the conductor in the region is shown in one of four graphs labelled (1) to (4), each plotting $B$ on the y-axis vs $r$ on the x-axis with $r=a$ marked: Graph (1) shows $B$ increasing linearly from 0 to a peak at $r=a$, then decreasing as a curve for $r>a$. Graph (2) shows $B=0$ for $r<a$, then jumping discontinuously to a peak at $r=a$ and decreasing for $r>a$. Graph (3) shows $B$ starting at a non-zero value, slightly decreasing with a kink at $r=a$, then continuing to decrease for $r>a$. Graph (4) shows $B$ increasing to a sharp peak exactly at $r=a$ (cusp shape) from both sides, decreasing for $r>a$ and increasing for $r<a$ in mirror fashion. Which plot correctly represents this variation?
questions.solution_text: For a long straight solid wire carrying steady current uniformly distributed across its cross-section: For $r < a$ (inside the wire), $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi a^2}$, so $B \propto r$ (linear increase from 0). For $r > a$ (outside the wire), $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, so $B \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$ (decreasing curve). This linear-then-inverse behaviour, peaking at $r=a$, matches Graph (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Forward Bias Current and Reverse Saturation Current
questions.question_text:
Two statements are given below:

A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly.

B. This current is called reverse saturation current.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statements A and B are true
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true

questions.solution_text: When the forward bias voltage increases beyond the threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly — statement A is true. However, this rapidly increasing forward current is NOT called the reverse saturation current (reverse saturation current is the small current that flows under reverse bias) — so statement B is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.

C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.

E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A is correct: the electrostatic field is zero inside a conductor. B is incorrect: the electric field at the surface is $\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\hat{n}$, which depends on surface charge density $\sigma$. C is correct: the interior of a charged conductor cannot have excess charge in the static situation. D is correct: the electrostatic field at the surface must be normal to the surface. E is incorrect: the electrostatic potential is constant (but can be non-zero) everywhere inside a charged conductor. So A, C and D are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does not give rise to the photoelectric effect? (Take Planck's constant as $6.6 \times 10^{-34}\,J\,s$)
questions.solution_text: Photoelectric effect does not occur when $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} <$ work function, i.e., $\lambda > \dfrac{hc}{W_0}$. $\lambda > \dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34} \times 3\times10^8}{6.6 \times 1.6\times10^{-19}} = \dfrac{3\times10^{-7}}{1.6} = \dfrac{300}{1.6}\,nm \approx 187.5\,nm$. So wavelengths greater than $187.5\,nm$ will not cause photoelectric emission. Among the options, $200\,nm > 187.5\,nm$, so option (3) 200 nm is correct (does not cause photoelectric effect).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Refraction of Ray Parallel to Principal Axis
questions.question_text: In a concave lens, a ray of light emanating from the object parallel to the principal axis of the lens after refraction:

options.text: passes through $2F$, which is the radius of curvature of the lens.
appears to diverge from the first principal focus.
emerges parallel to the principal axis.
passes through the second principal focus.

questions.solution_text: For a concave lens, a ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction, appears to diverge from the second principal focus $F_2$ (the virtual image position for an object at infinity). The given answer key marks option (2) as the 'best appropriate' answer, although strictly the correct description involves the second principal focus rather than the first principal focus as stated in the option text — this is noted as an official answer with an asterisk indicating ambiguity in the option wording.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of 100 atm. How deep can it go below the water surface? (Consider the density of water = $1000\,kg\,m^{-3}$, $1\,atm = 1 \times 10^5\,Pa$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10\,m/s^2$)
questions.solution_text: $P = P_0 + \rho gh \Rightarrow 100 \times 10^5 = 10^5 + 10^3 \times 10 \times h \Rightarrow 10^7 = 10^5 + 10^4 h \Rightarrow 10^3 = 10 + h \Rightarrow h = 1000 - 10 = 990\,m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Sources of Microwave, Visible, Gamma, Infrared Rays
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II: | List-I (Electromagnetic wave) | List-II (Production) | |---|---| | A. Microwave | I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level | | B. Visible light | II. Radioactive decay of nucleus | | C. Gamma rays | III. Vibration of atoms and molecules | | D. Infra-red rays | IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Microwaves are produced using Klystron valve or magnetron valve (A-IV). Visible light is produced when electrons in atoms emit light moving from higher to lower energy levels (B-I). Gamma rays are produced by radioactive decay of the nucleus (C-II). Infra-red rays are produced by vibration of atoms and molecules (D-III). So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Reagents for Reduction to Primary Amines
questions.question_text:
Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines.
A. (i) LiAlH4; (ii) H2O
B. Sn + HCl
C. H2/Ni
D. Na(Hg)/C2H5OH
E. Br2/aq. NaOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: Na(Hg)/C2H5OH reduces R-CN to R-CH2-NH2. LiAlH4 followed by H2O reduces R-CN to R-CH2-NH2. H2/Ni also reduces nitriles to primary amines. Sn+HCl reduces nitrile to aldehyde (R-CHO), not amine. Br2/aq. NaOH is the Hofmann bromamide reaction used for amides, not nitriles. So A, C and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List I (Transition metal/compound/complex) | List II (Catalytic Role) |
|---|---|
| A. V2O5 | I. Preparation of ammonia from N2/H2 mixture |
| B. Fe | II. Polymerisation of alkynes |
| C. PdCl2 | III. Preparation of H2SO4 and SO2 |
| D. Ni complex | IV. Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: V2O5 catalyses oxidation of SO2 to SO3 in manufacture of H2SO4 (III). Fe acts as catalyst in preparation of ammonia from N2/H2 mixture (I). PdCl2 catalyses oxidation of ethyne to ethanal (IV). Ni complex catalyses polymerisation of alkynes (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Calculating Delta G from Delta U and Delta S
questions.question_text: Consider the following reaction: 2A(g) + B(g) → 2D(g). $\Delta U^\ominus = -10\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S^\ominus = -44\,\text{JK}^{-1}$ at 298 K. Identify the correct option with $\Delta G^\ominus$ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K. (Given: R = 8.31 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$)
questions.solution_text: $\Delta n_g = 2 - (2+1) = -1$. $\Delta H^\ominus = \Delta U^\ominus + \Delta n_g RT = -10 - \frac{1 \times 298 \times 8.31}{1000} = -10 - 2.48 = -12.48\,\text{kJ/mol}$. $\Delta G^\ominus = \Delta H^\ominus - T\Delta S^\ominus = -12.48 - \frac{298 \times (-44)}{1000} = -12.48 + 13.112 = +0.632\,\text{kJ/mol}$. Since $\Delta G^\ominus > 0$, the reaction is non-spontaneous.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Identifying Orbitals from n and l Values
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List I (Quantum Numbers) | | List II (Orbital) |
|---|---|---|
| 'n' | 'l' | |
| A. 2 | 1 | I. 3d |
| B. 4 | 0 | II. 2p |
| C. 5 | 3 | III. 4s |
| D. 3 | 2 | IV. 5f |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: n=2, l=1 → 2p (II). n=4, l=0 → 4s (III). n=5, l=3 → 5f (IV). n=3, l=2 → 3d (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a qualitative analysis, Bi$^{3+}$ is detected by appearance of precipitate of BiO(OH)(s). Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298 K. BiO(OH)(s) $\rightleftharpoons$ BiO$^+$(aq) + OH$^-$(aq), K = 4 × 10$^{-10}$ (Given: log2 = 0.3010)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Secondary Structure of DNA and RNA
questions.question_text: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is

options.text: RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases

questions.solution_text: DNA has a double strand helix structure with four nitrogenous bases: adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and thymine (T). RNA is typically single stranded and contains uracil instead of thymine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is:
questions.solution_text: Metamerism arises due to different alkyl chains on either side of the same functional group in molecules of the same molecular formula. CH3OCH2CH2CH3 (methyl propyl ether) and CH3CH2OCH2CH3 (diethyl ether) are metamers — both have the molecular formula C4H10O with an ether linkage but different alkyl groups on each side.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List-I (Complex) | List-II (Type of isomerism) |
|---|---|
| A. [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] | I. Optical |
| B. [Co(en)3]3+ | II. Solvate |
| C. [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2 | III. Geometrical |
| D. [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 | IV. Linkage |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] shows geometrical isomerism (cis and trans) (III). [Co(en)3]3+ shows optical isomerism (I). [Co(NH3)5NO2]Cl2 and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]Cl2 are linkage isomers (IV). [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3 and [Cr(H2O)5Cl]Cl2·H2O are solvate isomers (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List-I (Order of reaction) | List-II (Unit of rate constant) |
|---|---|
| A. Zero order | I. mol$^{-1}$ L s$^{-1}$ |
| B. First order | II. mol$^{-2}$ L$^2$ s$^{-1}$ |
| C. Second order | III. s$^{-1}$ |
| D. Third order | IV. mol L$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: Unit of rate constant for nth order = (mol/L)^(1-n) s^(-1). Zero order (n=0): mol L^(-1) s^(-1) (IV). First order (n=1): s^(-1) (III). Second order (n=2): mol^(-1) L s^(-1) (I). Third order (n=3): mol^(-2) L^2 s^(-1) (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH2-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH3 is:
questions.solution_text: The longest carbon chain has 7 carbons (heptane). Numbering from the end that gives lowest locants: ethyl group at C3 and methyl group at C5. Substituents in alphabetical order: ethyl before methyl. So the IUPAC name is 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is 4.42 × 10$^{-19}$ J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.solution_text: Energy converted to light per second = 150 × 8/100 = 12 J. Number of photons = 12 / (4.42 × 10^(-19)) = 2.715 × 10^19 ≈ 2.71 × 10^19.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Methane reacts with steam at 1273 K in the presence of nickel catalyst to form:
questions.solution_text: CH4(g) + H2O(g) → CO + 3H2 (at 1273 K, Ni catalyst). This is the steam reforming reaction used for industrial preparation of dihydrogen gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Compound P(C8H8O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO3. Compounds P and Q, respectively, are:
questions.solution_text: P (C8H8O) with degree of unsaturation = (8+1) - 8/2 = 5 is a ketone (positive 2,4-DNP, negative Fehling's). Since drastic oxidation gives an aromatic dicarboxylic acid (effervescence with NaHCO3), P is 4-methylacetophenone (p-methyl acetophenone) and Q is benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (terephthalic acid). Answer 3 or 4 are considered correct by the official key.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Sigma and Pi Bonds in Molecules
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. C2H4 | I. 3 σ bonds, 2 π bonds |
| B. C2H2 | II. 3 σ bonds, one lone pair |
| C. CH4 | III. 4 σ bonds |
| D. NH3 | IV. 5 σ bonds, 1 π bond |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: C2H4 (H2C=CH2): 5 σ bonds (4 C-H + 1 C-C) and 1 π bond (IV). C2H2 (HC≡CH): 3 σ bonds and 2 π bonds (I). CH4: 4 σ bonds (III). NH3: 3 σ bonds and one lone pair (II). So A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The following two reactions give the same foul smelling product Z. C2H5Cl $\xrightarrow{X}$ Z and C2H5CNH2 $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3/\text{ethanolic KOH}}$ Z. X and Z, respectively, are:
questions.solution_text: C2H5Cl + AgCN → C2H5NC (isocyanide, foul smelling) [AgCN reacts through N to give isocyanide]. C2H5CNH2 → (Br2/NaOH) → C2H5NH2 (Hofmann degradation) → (CHCl3/KOH) → C2H5NC (carbylamine reaction). Both give C2H5NC. So X = AgCN, Z = C2H5NC.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5.4 g of urea is: (Given: Molar mass of urea: 60 g mol$^{-1}$; NA: 6.022 × 10$^{23}$ particles mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution_text: Urea: H2N-CO-NH2 has 4 H atoms. Moles of urea = 5.4/60 = 0.09 mol. Number of H atoms = 0.09 × 4 × 6.022 × 10^23 = 2.168 × 10^23.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:

options.text: Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals.
Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen.

questions.solution_text: Both nitrogen and oxygen do not contain d-orbitals, so nitrogen cannot form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen. Statement 4 is incorrect. Phosphorus and arsenic can form dπ-dπ bonds with transition metals through their vacant d-orbitals. P, As and Sb show catenation. N can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself (N≡N).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand?
questions.solution_text: An ambidentate ligand has two different donor atoms and either can coordinate. Thiocyanate (SCN–) can coordinate through S (thiocyanato) or N (isothiocyanato). Ethane-1,2-diamine and oxalate are bidentate. EDTA is hexadentate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is
questions.solution_text: Metallic character decreases across a period (left to right) and increases down a group. Electronegativity values: Na(0.9) < Mg(1.2) < Be(1.5) < Si(1.8) < P(2.1). Higher electronegativity means lower metallic character. So increasing metallic character: P < Si < Be < Mg < Na.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II (conversions of organic compounds with reagents):
| List I | List II |
|---|---|
| A. Cumene → Phenol | I. (i) Oleum; (ii) NaOH, Δ; (iii) H+ |
| B. CH3COOH → CH3CH2OH | II. (i) O2; (ii) H2O/H+ |
| C. CH3CH2CH2OH → CH3CH(OH)CH3 (then further to product) | III. (i) CH3OH, H+; (ii) H2, catalyst |
| D. Benzene → Phenol | IV. (i) conc. H2SO4, Δ; (ii) H+/H2O |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: Cumene → Phenol uses O2 followed by H2O/H+ (II). CH3COOH → CH3CH2OH uses (i) CH3OH, H+ (to form ester) then (ii) H2, catalyst (reduction) (III). CH3CH2CH2OH → via dehydration then Markovnikov hydration gives (CH3)2CHOH, using conc. H2SO4, Δ then H+/H2O (IV). Benzene → Phenol via sulfonation: Oleum, NaOH/Δ, H+ (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Although +3 oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows +4 oxidation state because:

options.text: After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f$^{14}$ electronic configuration.
Its nearest inert gas is Radon.
After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f$^0$ electronic configuration.

questions.solution_text: Ce is [Xe]4f15d16s2. In +3 state it is [Xe]4f1. In +4 state it loses the 4f1 electron to achieve [Xe] 4f0 configuration, which is extra stable (empty f subshell). Hence Ce shows +4 oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Reactions of Alcohols with Phosphorus Halides
questions.subtopic: Reaction Sequence with PCl5 and KOH
questions.question_text: In the following reaction sequence, X and Z respectively are: CH3CH2CH2-OH + PCl5 → CH3CH2CH2Cl + X + HCl; CH3CH2CH2Cl $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}/\Delta}$ Y $\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}/(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO})_2\text{O}_2}$ Z
questions.solution_text: CH3CH2CH2OH + PCl5 → CH3CH2CH2Cl + POCl3 + HCl. So X = POCl3. CH3CH2CH2Cl + alc. KOH/Δ → CH3CH=CH2 (Y, propene by elimination). CH3CH=CH2 + HBr/(C6H5CO)2O2 (peroxide) → anti-Markovnikov addition → CH3CH2CH2Br (Z). So X = POCl3, Z = CH3CH2CH2Br.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
| List I (Complex/ion) | List II (Shape/geometry) |
|---|---|
| A. [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2] | (I) Octahedral |
| B. [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 | (II) Trigonal bipyramidal |
| C. [NiCl4]2– | (III) Square planar |
| D. [Fe(CO)5] | (IV) Tetrahedral |
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2]: Pt has dsp2 hybridisation → square planar (III). [Co(NH3)6]Cl3: Co has d2sp3 hybridisation → octahedral (I). [NiCl4]2–: Ni has sp3 hybridisation → tetrahedral (IV). [Fe(CO)5]: sp3d hybridisation → trigonal bipyramidal (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is:
questions.solution_text: Phthalein dye test: phenol heated with phthalic anhydride in presence of concentrated H2SO4 forms phenolphthalein (colourless). On treatment with NaOH it gives a pink colour. This test specifically identifies the phenolic (-OH on benzene ring) functional group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Two products X and Y are formed in the following reaction sequence: Benzene + CH3Cl $\xrightarrow{\text{Anhy. AlCl}_3}$ W $\xrightarrow{\text{dil. HNO}_3 + \text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{warm}}$ X + Y. The suitable method that can be used for the separation of products X and Y is:
questions.solution_text: Benzene + CH3Cl → toluene (W) by Friedel-Crafts alkylation. Toluene + mild HNO3/H2SO4 gives ortho-nitrotoluene (X, b.p. 222°C) and para-nitrotoluene (Y, b.p. 238°C, m.p. 54°C). These are separated by fractional distillation under reduced pressure since they have different boiling points.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Molality, Molarity, Henry's Law, Mole Fraction
questions.question_text:
Identify the correct statements:
A. The molality of 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass: 60 g mol$^{-1}$) in 75 g of benzene solution is 0.556 m.
B. The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH (molar mass: 40 g mol$^{-1}$) in 450 mL of solution is 0.278 M at 298 K.
C. Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
D. The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
E. For a binary mixture of A and B, the mole fraction of B will be $x_B = \dfrac{n_A}{n_A+n_B}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution_text: A: m = (2.5/60) × (1000/75) = 0.556 m ✓. B: M = (5/40) × (1000/450) = 0.278 M ✓. C: Correct — cold water holds more dissolved O2 (Henry's law: KH ∝ T, so solubility ∝ 1/T). D: Incorrect — solubility of gas increases with increase in pressure (Henry's law: P = KH×X). E: Incorrect — mole fraction of B = nB/(nA+nB), not nA/(nA+nB). So A, B and C are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: During Lassaigne's test, the elements present in an organic compound are converted from:
questions.solution_text: In Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. The elements present in covalent form (C, H, N, S, halogens) in the organic compound are converted into ionic form (NaCN, Na2S, NaX) in the sodium fusion extract. So conversion is from covalent form to ionic form.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is: (Given: Molar mass of Cu = 63 g mol$^{-1}$; 1 F = 96487 C mol$^{-1}$)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, 500 J is absorbed by the system and work of 200 J is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is:
questions.solution_text: By first law: ΔU = q + w. q = +500 J (absorbed), w = –200 J (work done by system). ΔU = 500 + (–200) = 300 J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Zero Order Reaction - Concentration vs Time Graph
questions.question_text: For a certain reaction R → Product, the plot of concentration [R] vs time has a negative slope (linear) as shown. The order of reaction is:
questions.solution_text: For zero order reaction: [R] = [R0] – kt, which is a linear equation with negative slope k. A linear [R] vs time plot indicates zero order reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the correct statement about ClF3 from the following options:

options.text: It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.

questions.solution_text: ClF3: Cl has 7 valence electrons, forms 3 bonds with F, so has 2 lone pairs. Total electron pairs = 5 (sp3d hybridisation). Shape based on VSEPR: 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs → T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Identification of Anions using Dilute H2SO4
questions.question_text: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute H2SO4 was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following:
questions.solution_text: CH3COO– + H2SO4 → CH3COOH (acetic acid — smell of vinegar, colourless vapours, acidic — turns blue litmus red). Sulphide gives smell of rotten eggs (H2S). Carbonate gives CO2 (odourless). Sulphate gives no gas with dilute H2SO4. So acetate (CH3COO–) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
